quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: On a four-lane road, you do not need to stop for a stopped school bus if you are traveling in the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: On a four-lane or wider highway, you must stop for a school bus only when traveling behind it. Always drive with caution near children.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go.
Stop, look both ways, and then proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Ease off the gas, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: Can you pass on a two-lane road if there is a single solid yellow line on your side?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You may only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with no lights or gates?

options.text: Cross the tracks fast.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train comes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at crossings without lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 or older, what blood alcohol level is illegal?

options.text: 0.05 percent
0.08 percent
0.02 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, driving with a blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If a cyclist is in your lane and you want to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Treat the cyclist like any other driver you would pass.
Tap your horn lightly to alert the cyclist.
Wait for clear traffic, change lanes, and pass the cyclist.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Bikes are vehicles and should be treated like other traffic. Use your horn lightly to get attention, not to startle. Change lanes when traffic is clear; do not squeeze past them.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: Toward the center of the road.
Toward the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. This helps you stay on your lane. Do not retaliate by keeping your lights bright.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When passing, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough space before moving back into your lane. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your mirror, it is safe to return to the driving lane.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line dividing it. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic moves in both directions.
Traffic moves in one direction only.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay left of the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower cars when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the fastest speed you may drive?

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe for conditions.
A speed that matches current road and weather conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never drive faster than the speed limit or faster than is safe for conditions. Adjust your speed based on traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and lighting.

questions.question: When must you give the right-of-way to a pedestrian?

options.text: When they are in a marked crosswalk.
When they are in any crosswalk or at an intersection.
Whenever they are crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever they are crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, yield to pedestrians crossing any street.

questions.question: You are driving on a four-lane highway and see a stopped school bus with red lights flashing on the opposite side of the road. What should you do?

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass only if a pedestrian signals that it is safe.
You can pass because you do not need to stop.
You must turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass because you do not need to stop.
questions.explanation: On a four-lane highway, you only need to stop for a school bus if you are coming from behind it. You may pass if the bus is on the opposite side of the road.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol level can your license be suspended if you are under 21?

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 have zero tolerance for alcohol. Any amount of alcohol in your system can result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is coming up.
You are entering a construction area.
You must turn left soon.
The road will become narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will become narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid edge line marks the boundary of the travel lane. When the edge line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: Is it against the law for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles may share a lane, but a car must never share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is correct?

options.text: They can be moving or stationary.
They are marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down in work zones.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving (like stripe painting or snow removal). They use orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of traffic light colors?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights always arrange from top to bottom as red, yellow, and green. This warns drivers about signals ahead at an intersection.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a dangerous situation. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you, first take your foot off the gas. This gives you more space without requiring hard braking or swerving into another lane.

questions.question: Your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). If you need to stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal down.
Pump the brakes firmly and repeatedly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes firmly and repeatedly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop in an emergency. Your car will stop quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have gone off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, let off the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes hard and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, let off the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, let off the gas, and gently brake. Slow down and check for traffic. Look for a safe place to merge back onto the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly, as this can cause you to lose control or hit other lanes.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should stay at least three to four seconds behind the vehicle in front of you under normal conditions.
As you drive faster, you should follow closer.
Following distance only matters on snow and ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should stay at least three to four seconds behind the vehicle in front of you under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: Keep a three or four second gap between your vehicle and the one in front of you at all times. If conditions are bad, such as rain or heavy traffic, increase this distance.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Let the vehicle on your left go first.
Let the vehicle on your right go first.
Wait until all vehicles are gone before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or signals, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. After that, vehicles proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars keep passing you on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On an interstate highway, if you are driving slower than traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Your vehicle's gas pedal gets stuck open while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Slam on the brakes.
Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, your vehicle will keep going. Turn off the ignition by moving only the ignition switch just enough to stop the engine, not to lock the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using its siren or lights. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is behind you without its siren or lights on, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Workers ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and warn drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that a sharp turn is coming and you should slow down.

questions.question: When can you park on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: Anytime you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from traffic.
